title: Integral Estimator
description: Numerically integrate any expression over [a, b] with Simpson's, trapezoidal or midpoint rule — real quadrature with the formula and error behavior shown.
howto: Type the integrand as a function of x, e.g. sin(x) + x^2.
Enter the limits a and b and the number of subintervals n.
Choose Simpson's, trapezoidal or midpoint rule and press Integrate.
Read the estimate, the exact formula applied, and how the value converges as n grows.

faqs.a: Simpson's rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 3 and usually converges fastest (error ~ 1/n⁴). The tool shows all three side by side so you can compare.

faqs.q: Why must n be even for Simpson's rule?
faqs.a: Simpson's rule fits parabolas over pairs of subintervals, so it needs an even count. The tool rounds an odd n up and tells you.
Polynomials (x^2), sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, exp, ln, log (base 10), sqrt, abs, pi, e, and the usual + − * / ^ operators with parentheses.
